title: AWS IAM S3Browser LoginProfile Creation
id: 62b0e2a7-3c6f-440d-b429-344442044001
status: test
description: Detects S3 Browser utility performing reconnaissance looking for existing IAMUsers without a LoginProfile defined then (when found) creating an LoginProfile.
references:
    - https://github.com/elastic/detection-rules/blob/221012-security-orchestrator-integrations/rules/integrations/aws/cloudtrail/privilege_escalation_s3browser_loginprofile_creation.toml
author: Austin Songer @austinsonger
date: 2022-08-15
modified: 2023-02-03
tags:
    - attack.privilege-escalation
    - attack.persistence
    - attack.initial-access
    - attack.execution
    - attack.stealth
    - attack.t1059.009
    - attack.t1078.004
logsource:
    product: aws
    service: cloudtrail
detection:
    selection:
        eventSource: 'iam.amazonaws.com'
        eventName: 'CreateLoginProfile'
    filter_main_valid_user:

    condition: selection and not 1 of filter_main_*
falsepositives:
    - Valid usage of S3 Browser for IAM LoginProfile listing and / or creation
level: high

title: New CA Policy by Non-approved Actor
id: 206379a1-2b2f-4c6e-b422-044400000000

description: Monitor and alert on conditional access changes.

    - https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/architecture/security-operations-privileged-accounts#conditional-access-policy-changes
author: Mark Morowczynski '@markmorow', Gloria Lee, '@gleeiamglo'

    - attack.t1548

    product: azure
    service: auditlogs

    selection:
        properties.message: 'Conditional Access policy created.'
    filter_main_admin:
        properties.userType: 'Administrators'
    filter_main_service_principal:
        properties.userType: 'Service Principal'
    filter_main_system:
        properties.userType: 'System'
    filter_main_automation:
        properties.userType: 'Automation Account'
    filter_main_azure_devops:
        properties.userType: 'Azure DevOps'
    filter_main_azure_pipelines:
        properties.userType: 'Azure Pipelines'
    filter_main_azure_sql:

title: Binary Padding - Linux
id: 645839a7-2b7f-4e7c-b42d-244204000000
status: test
description: |
    Adversaries may use binary padding to add junk data and alter the on-disk representation of malware.
    This rule detect using dd and truncate to add a junk data file.
references:
    - https://github.com/redcanaryco/atomic-red-team/blob/f339e7da7d05f6057fdfcdd3742bfcf365fee2a9/atomics/T1027.001/T1027.001.md#atomic-test-1---binary-padding-linux
author: frack113
date: 2022-01-01
modified: 2023-02-03
tags:
    - attack.stealth
    - attack.t1027.001
logsource:
    product: linux
    service: auditd
detection:
    selection:
        type: 'EXECVE'
        a0|contains: '/bin/dd'
        a1|contains: 'if=/dev/zero'
        a2|contains: 'of='
    filter_main_truncate:
        a0|contains: '/usr/bin/truncate'
        a1|contains: '-s'
    condition: selection and not 1 of filter_main_*
falsepositives:
    - Unknown
level: high

title: Masquerading as Linux Crond Process
id: 725489a1-2b8f-4c6e-b42d-244220220021
status: test
description: |
    Masquerading occurs when the name or location of an executable,
    legitimate or malicious, is manipulated or abused for the sake
    of evading defenses and observation.
    Several different variations of this technique have been observed.
references:
    - https://github.com/redcanaryco/atomic-red-team/blob/f339e7da7d05f6057fdfcdd3742bfcf365fee2a9/atomics/T1036.003/T1036.003.md#atomic-test-1---masquerading-as-linux-cron-process
author: frack113
date: 2022-01-01
modified: 2023-02-16
tags:
    - attack.stealth
    - attack.t1036.003
logsource:
    product: linux
    service: auditd
detection:
    selection:
        type: 'EXECVE'
        a0|contains: '/crond'
    filter_main_legit:
        a0|endswith: '/crond'
    condition: selection and not 1 of filter_main_*
falsepositives:
    - Legitimate crond process
level: medium

status: test
description: |
    Detects a Windows Filtering Platform (WFP) blocked connection even involving common Endpoint Detection and Response (EDR) agents.
    Adversaries may use WFP filters to prevent Endpoint Detection an Response (EDR) agents from reporting security events.
references:
    - https://github.com/redcanaryco/atomic-red-team/blob/f339e7da7d05f6057fdfcdd3742bfcf365fee2a9/atomics/T1685/T1685.md#atomic-test-1---wfp-filter-blocks-connection-from-edr-agent-binary

date: 2022-01-01
modified: 2023-02-03
tags:
    - attack.defense-impairment
    - attack.t1685
logsource:
    product: windows
    service: security
    definition: 'Requirements: Audit Filtering Platform Connection needs to be enabled'
detection:
    selection:
        EventID: 5156 # A filter blocked a connection attempt
        FilterName|contains:
            - 'Microsoft-Windows-WFP-FilteringPlatform'
            - 'Microsoft-Windows-WFP-FilteringEngine'
    filter_main_edr_agent:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\Endpoint Protection\EndpointProtection.exe' # Microsoft Defender Antivirus
            - '\Endpoint Protection\mpengine.exe' # Microsoft Defender Antivirus
            - '\ElasticAgent.exe' # Elastic
            - '\FireEye\Agent\agent.exe' # FireEye
            - '\Kaspersky\KAV\KavService.exe' # Kaspersky
            - '\McAfee\Endpoint Security\mcasvc.exe' # McAfee
            - '\Nextron Systems\Nextron Systems Agent\NextronSystemsAgent.exe' # Nextron Systems
            - '\Palo Alto Networks\Threat Prevention\pantsvc.exe' # Palo Alto Networks
            - '\Symantec\Symantec Endpoint Protection\Symantec Endpoint Protection Manager\sepeng.exe' # Symantec
            - '\VMware\vSphere Client\vmwarevpxd.exe' # VMware vSphere
            - '\Zscaler\Zscaler Agent\zagent.exe' # Zscaler
    condition: selection and not 1 of filter_main_*
falsepositives:
    - Unlikely
level: high
regression_tests_path: regression_data/rules/windows/security/audit_wfp_blocked_connection/info.yml

description: Detects the usage of particular AttributeLDAPDisplayNames, which ae known for data exchange via LDAP by the tool LDAPF ragger and are additionally not commonly used in companies.
references:

author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

modified: 2023-02-03

logsource:
    product: windows
    service: security
    definition: 'The "Audit Directory Service Changes" logging policy must be configured in order to receive events. '
    # Audit events are generated only for objects with configured system access
    # control lists (SACLs). Audit events are generated
    # only for objects with configured system access control lists (SACLS) and only when accessed in a manner that matches their SACLS settings.
    # This policy covers the following events ids - 5141. Note that the default policy
    # does not cover User objects. For that a custom AuditRul e need to be setup (See https://github.com/ OTRF/Set-AuditRule)
level: high

    selection:
        EventID:
            - 5136 # The directory service is starting.
            - 5137 # A new object was created.
            - 5138 # An existing object was deleted.
            - 5139 # An existing object was renamed.
            - 5141 # An attribute was changed.
    filter_main_generic:
        # Note: You can add more attributes here if you have them in your environment
        # Example: AttributeLDAPDisplayName: 'employeeNumber'
        AttributeLDAPDisplayName|endswith:
            - 'departmentNumber'
            - 'employeeNumber'
            - 'employeeType'
            - 'labeledURI'
            - 'mail'
            - 'mobile'
            - 'objectGUID'
            - 'postalCode'
            - 'st'
            - 'street'
            - 'telephoneNumber'
            - 'thumbnailPhoto'
            - 'userPrincipalName'
    condition: selection and not 1 of filter_main_*

title: Possible Shadow Credentials Added
id: 20f1a1c0-3b2e-440d-b481-344424424222
status: test
description: Detects possible addition of shadow credentials to an active directory object.
references:
    - https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/security/blog/2022/09/13/microsoft-security-advisory-microsoft-365-customer-facing-accounts-compromised-by-actors-linked-to-russia/
author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)
date: 2022-09-14
modified: 2023-02-03
tags:
    - attack.persistence
    - attack.credential-access
    - attack.defense-impairment
    - attack.t1556
logsource:
    product: windows
    service: security
    definition: 'The "Audit Directory Service Changes" logging policy must be configured in order to receive events. '
    # Audit events are generated only for objects with configured system access
    # control lists (SACLs). Audit events are generated
    # only for objects with configured system access control lists (SACLS) and only when accessed in a manner that matches their SACLS settings.
    # This policy covers the following events ids - 5141. Note that the default policy
    # does not cover User objects. For that a custom Audit Rule need to be setup (See https://github.com/ OTRF /Set-AuditRule)
level: high
detection:
    selection:
        EventID: 5141
        ObjectTypeName: 'User'
        PropertyName: 'msDS-AllowedToDelegateTo'
        NewValue|contains: 'http://schemas.microsoft.com/activedirectory/crossdomaindelegation/'
    condition: selection
falsepositives:
    - Modifications in the msDS-KeyCredentialLink attribute can be done legitimatly by the Azure AD Connect synchronization account or the ADFS
      service account. These accounts can be added as Exceptions. From elastic FP section
# Note: The Elastic version of this rule is available at https://github.com/elastic/detection-rules/blob/master/rules/windows/registry/registry_key_credential_link_addition.yml
regression_tests_path: regression_data/rules/windows/security/audit_directory_service_changes/registry_key_credential_link_addition/info.yml

status: test

    Detects file access requests to the the Windows Data Protection API Main keys by an uncommon application.
    This can be a sign of credential stealing. Example case would b usage of mimikatz "dpapi::masterkey" function
references:
    - https://github.com/redcanaryco/atomic-red-team/blob/f339e7da7d05f6057fdfcdd3742bfcf365fee2a9/atomics/T1555.004/T1555.004.md#atomic-test-1---access-to-windows-dpapi-master-keys-by-uncommon-applications

title: DLL Load By System Process From Suspicious Locations
id: 958b0c0e-2a7f-440d-b42d-044440444044
status: test
description: Detects when a system process (i.e. located in sys32, syswow64, etc.) loads an DLL from a suspicious location or a location with permissive permission such as "C:\Users\Public"
references:
    - https://github.com/redcanaryco/atomic-red-team/blob/f339e7da7d05f6057fdfcdd3742bfcf365fee2a9/atomics/T1070/T1070.md#atomic-test-1---dll-injection-via-image-load-event
author: frack113
date: 2022-01-01
modified: 2023-02-03
tags:
    - attack.stealth
    - attack.t1070
logsource:
    product: windows
    category: image_load
detection:
    selection:
        Image|endswith:
            # Note: Add more locations if you see them in your environment
            - '\calc.exe'
            - '\cmd.exe'
            - '\mshta.exe'
            - '\powershell_ise.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
            - '\regsvr32.exe'
            - '\rundll32.exe'
            - '\wscript.exe'
            - '\wmic.exe'
            - '\wsl.exe'
            - '\winword.exe'
            - '\write.exe'
            - '\wscript.exe'
            - ':\Windows\System32\'
            - ':\Windows\SysWOW64\'
            - ':\Windows\WinSxS\'
            - ':\Windows\Temp\'
            - ':\Windows\Tracing\'
            - ':\Windows\Tasks\'
            - ':\Windows\PerfLogs\'
            - ':\Windows\Prefetch\'
            - ':\Windows\Fonts\'
            - ':\Windows\IME\'
            - ':\Windows\Help\'
            - ':\Windows\Media\'
            - ':\Windows\servicing\Packages\'
            - ':\Windows\SoftwareDistribution\'
            - ':\Windows\Setup\OfflineContent\'
            - ':\Windows\Temp\'
        ImageLoaded|contains:
            - ':\Users\Public\'
            - ':\Users\Default\'
            - ':\Users\All Users\'
            - ':\ProgramData\'
            - ':\Windows\Temp\'
    filter_main_system32:
        ImageLoaded|startswith: ':\Windows\System32\'
    filter_main_syswow64:
        ImageLoaded|startswith: ':\Windows\SysWOW64\'
    filter_main_win_sxs:
        ImageLoaded|startswith: ':\Windows\WinSxS\'
    filter_optional_temp:
        ImageLoaded|startswith: ':\Windows\Temp\'
    filter_optional_programdata:
        ImageLoaded|startswith: ':\ProgramData\'
    filter_optional_users_public:
        ImageLoaded|startswith: ':\Users\Public\'
    filter_optional_users_default:
        ImageLoaded|startswith: ':\Users\Default\'
    filter_optional_users_allusers:
        ImageLoaded|startswith: ':\Users\All Users\'
    filter_optional_windows_setup_offlinecontent:
        ImageLoaded|startswith: ':\Windows\Setup\OfflineContent\'
    filter_optional_windows_softwaredistribution:
        ImageLoaded|startswith: ':\Windows\SoftwareDistribution\'
    filter_optional_windows_servicing_packages:
        ImageLoaded|startswith: ':\Windows\servicing\Packages\'
    filter_optional_windows_tracing:
        ImageLoaded|startswith: ':\Windows\Tracing\'
    filter_optional_windows_prefetch:
        ImageLoaded|startswith: ':\Windows\Prefetch\'
    filter_optional_windows_fonts:
        ImageLoaded|startswith: ':\Windows\Fonts\'
    filter_optional_windows_ime:
        ImageLoaded|startswith: ':\Windows\IME\'
    filter_optional_windows_help:
        ImageLoaded|startswith: ':\Windows\Help\'
    filter_optional_windows_media:

status: test
description: |
    Detects an executable initiating a network connection to "ngrok" domains.
    Attackers were seen using this "ngrok" in order to store their second stage payloads and malware.
    While communication with such domains can be legitimate, often times is sign of either data exfiltration by malicious actors or addition download.

    - https://www.ngrok.com/

date: 2023-08-04
tags:
    - attack.command-and-control
    - attack.exfiltration
    - attack.t1102
    - attack.t1567
    - attack.t1572
logsource:
    category: network_connection
    product: windows
detection:
    selection:
        DestinationHostname|contains: '.ngrok.io'
    filter_main_legit_domains:
        DestinationHostname|endswith:
            - '.ngrok.io'
            - '.ngrok-free.app'
    condition: selection and not 1 of filter_main_*
falsepositives:
    - Legitimate use of the ngrok service.
level: high

title: Security Software Discovery Via Powershell Script
id: 924367a1-3b1e-4f3c-b429-044204200000
status: test
description: |
    Detects calls to "get-process" where the output is piped to a "where-object" filter to search for security solution processes.
    Adversaries may attempt to get a listing of security software configurations, defensive tools, and sensors that are installed on
    a system or in a cloud environment. This may include firewalls, anti-virus, etc.
references:
    - https://github.com/redcanaryco/atomic-red-team/blob/f339e7da7d05f6057fdfcdd3742bfcf365fee2a9/atomics/T1518.001/T1518.001.md#atomic-test-1---security-software-discovery-via-powershell-script
author: frack113
date: 2022-01-01
modified: 2023-02-03
tags:
    - attack.discovery
    - attack.t1518.001
logsource:
    product: windows
    category: ps_script
    definition: 'Requirements: Script Block Logging must be enabled'
detection:
    selection_cmdlet:
        ScriptBlockText|contains|all:
            - 'Get-Process'
            - '| Where-Object '
    selection_filter:
        ScriptBlockText|contains:
            - '-Name *av*'
            - '-Name *firewall*'
            - '-Name *antivirus*'
            - '-Name *defender*'
            - '-Name *endpoint*
    condition: all of selection_*
falsepositives:
    - False positives might occur due to the nature of the ScriptBlockBeing ingested as a big blob. Initial tuning is required.
    - As the "selection_cmdlet" is common in scripts the matching engine might slow down the seach. Change into regex or a more accurate string to avoid hevy resource consumption if experienced
level: medium
regression_tests_path: regression_data/rules/windows/powershell/powershell_script/posh_ps_security_software_discovery/info.yml

public static extern IntPtr OpenProcess(uint dwDesiredAccess, int bInheritHandle, uint dwProcessId);'

title: Potential Arbitrary Command Execution Via FTP.EXE
id: 34678c0a-2b1e-4f9d-b42d-044204000000
status: test
description: Detects execution of "ftp.exe" script with the "-s" or "/s" flag and any child processes ran by "ftp.exe".
references:
    - https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/security/blog/2022/08/18/microsoft-security-advisory-30119-001-remote-code-execution-vulnerability-in-microsoft-exchange-server/
author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)
date: 2022-08-22
modified: 2023-02-03
tags:
    - attack.execution
    - attack.stealth
    - attack.t1059
    - attack.t1202
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_img:
        - Image|endswith: '\ftp.exe'
        - OriginalFileName: 'FTP.EXE'
    selection_cli:
        CommandLine|contains:
            - '-s:'
            - '/s '
    filter_main_legit_parent:
        ParentImage|endswith:
            - '\cmd.exe'
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
            - '\wsl.exe'
            - '\wslhost.exe'
    filter_main_legit_child:
        # Note: The parent image is set to null because we don't want to add more complexity here. We can always add it back if needed
        ParentCommandLine|contains:
            - ' -s '
            - ' /s '
    filter_optional_legit_parent:
        ParentImage|endswith:
        - '\msiexec.exe'
        - '\regsvr32.exe'
        - '\rundll32.exe'
        - '\wscript.exe'
        - '\cscript.exe'
    filter_optional_legit_child:
        # Note: The parent image and command line are set to null because we don't want to add more complex logic here. We can always add them back if needed
        ParentCommandLine|contains:
            # Example: C:\Windows\System32\ftp.exe -s:C:\Users\Public\Temp\test.txt
            - ' -s:'
            - ' /s '
    condition: all of selection_* and not 1 of filter_main_* and not 1 of filter_optional_*
falsepositives:
    - Unknown
level: medium

title: Suspicious Shells Spawn by Java Utility Keytool
id: 30254681-79a1-4b8c-bf3d-224022402240
status: test
description: Detects suspicious shell spawn from Java utility keytool process (eg. adselfservice plus exploitation)
references:
    - https://www.crowdstrike.com/blog/attacking-active-directory-with-adselfservice/
author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)
date: 2023-01-16
modified: 2023-02-13
tags:
    - attack.initial-access
    - attack.persistence
    - attack.privilege-escalation
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_img:
        - Image|endswith: '\keytool.exe'
        - OriginalFileName: 'keytool.exe'

        CommandLine|contains|all:
            - '-genkeypair'
            - '-alias'
            - '-keystore'
            - '-storepass'
            - '-keyalg'
            - '-keysize'
            - '-validity'
            - '-dname'

    filter_optional_java_19:
        ParentCommandLine|contains: 'C:\ProgramFiles\Java\jdk-19\bin\java.exe'
    filter_optional_java_20:
        ParentCommandLine|contains: 'C:\Programdata\Oracle\Java\javapath\java.exe' # Note: This is the same as the previous filter but with a different path
    filter_optional_java_21:
        ParentCommandLine|contains: 'C:\Programfiles\Java\jdk-21\bin\java.exe'
    filter_optional_java_8:
        ParentCommandLine|contains: 'C:\Windows\system32\java.exe'
    filter_optional_java_9:
        ParentCommandLine|contains: 'C:\Windows\System32\java.exe'
    filter_optional_java_10:
        ParentCommandLine|contains: 'C:\Windows\SysWOW64\java.exe'
    filter_optional_java_11:
        ParentCommandLine|contains: 'C:\Windows\syswow64\java.exe'
    filter_optional_java_22:
        ParentCommandLine|contains: 'C:\Program files\Java\jdk-22\bin\java.exe'
    filter_optional_java_64bit:
        ParentCommandLine|contains: 'C:\Program_files\Java\jre64\bin\java.exe'
    filter_optional_java_32bit:
        ParentCommandLine|contains: 'C:\Windows\systools\java.exe'
    filter_optional_java_32_1:
        ParentCommandLine|contains: 'C:\windows\system32\java.exe'
    filter_optional_java_other:
        ParentCommandLine|contains:
            - 'C:\Program Files\Common Files\Oracle\Java\javapath\java.exe '

        ParentCommandLine|contains: 'C:\Windows\PUBLIC\Temp\java.exe'
    filter_optional_java_13:
        ParentCommandLine|contains: 'C:\Users\Public\Temp\java.exe'
    filter_optional_java_23:
        ParentCommandLine|contains: 'C:\Program data\Oracle\Java\javapath\java.exe'

    condition: all of selection_* and not 1 of filter_main_* and not 1 of filter_optional_*

    - Unknown
level: high

title: WMI Persistence - Script Event Consumer
id: 7289b2a7-2c6f-4e7d-b487-244240000000
status: test
description: |
    Detects the execution of a script event consumer. When scrcon.exe launches, it does so in response to the creation
    of an ActiveScriptEventConsumer instance and will execute registered JScript or VBScript code as a
    result. Script event consumers are a built-in Windows Management Instrumentation (WMi) class that automatically
    executes a predefined script (in VBScript or JScript)
    whenever a specific system event occurs. Adversaries often abuse script event consumers to maintain persistence
    on a compromised host by executing a malicious script whenever a specific event occurs.
references:

title: Enable LM Hash Storage
id: 9456387f-2a7c-4b7e-b481-244404000000
status: test
description: |
    Detects changes to the "NoLMHash" registry value in order to allow Windows to store LM Hashses.
    By setting this registry value to "0" (DWORD), Windows will be allowed to store a LANmanager hash of your password in Active Directory and local SAM databases.
references:
    - https://www.cisa.gov/uscert/ncas/alerts/aa21-027a
author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)
date: 2021-06-08
modified: 2023-02-03
tags:
    - attack.persistence
    - attack.defense-impairment
    - attack.t1112
logsource:
    product: windows
    category: registry_set
detection:
    selection:
        TargetObject|contains: '\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Lsa\NoLMHash'
        Details: 'DWORD (0x00000000)'
    condition: selection
falsepositives:
    - Unknown
level: high
